@@k15@@
Part 15

Gaps, open questions and the self-check

What could not be established, and how to turn it into a question.

Why this section exists@@x-why@@

A pack that hides what it could not find is more dangerous than one that admits it. Everything below was searched for and not established from public sources between 11 and 12 October 2026. Do not fill these gaps with guesses in an interview. Several make excellent questions to ask instead.

Source uncertain: research limits

The research hit a shared web-search limit partway through four workstreams. Where that happened the researchers switched to direct fetches of primary documents (SEC filings, KKR's own job board and people directory, Companies House), so the core numbers are strong. Trade press, LinkedIn, Glassdoor, Wall Street Oasis and The Student Room were thinly covered; forum material appears only as search snippets and is labelled as anecdote.

About KCS and the team@@x-kcs@@

  • No named "Head of KCS EMEA". KKR's directory shows no one with that title. The closest is Mark Danzey, European Head of KCM and European Head of Institutional Client Solutions. Reporting lines in every org chart in this pack are reconstructed, not published.
  • Junior headcount. KKR's directory lists Principal level and above only. All KCS EMEA and London headcounts are estimates with a method shown, not counts.
  • Client numbers. KKR does not disclose how many LPs it has, how many invest in more than one strategy, or its re-up rate. The 2024 Investor Day deck, which may contain such a slide, could not be retrieved.
  • Private wealth target. No single KKR-published private wealth AUM target or wealth capital-raised figure was found; only K-Series AUM and flows.
  • Europe vehicles. No named KKR ELTIF or UK LTAF was confirmed. K-PRIME is confirmed as the Luxembourg twin of K-PEC. K-PRIME, KREST and K-FITS launch dates and per-vehicle AUM were not extracted.
  • Capital Group U.S. Equity+. Filed July 2025 for an "early 2026" launch; the actual launch was not confirmed.
  • Career moves. No public example of someone moving from KCS into an investing seat was found.
  • Tools. Salesforce is confirmed in KKR postings. DealCloud, eVestment and data-room vendors were not confirmed.
  • Names to avoid. "Alisa Amarosa Wood" appears in a 2023 press quote but is not in KKR's current KCS directory. Do not present any person's current title unless it is confirmed on kkr.com.

About the application and interview@@x-process@@

  • The SEO London application form (questions, word limits, cover letter or not) sits behind a student login and could not be read. Screenshot it and draft answers offline.
  • The London summer process. No public report of KKR's London summer intern interview process was found. Whether there is an online test, a HireVue, or a superday in London is unconfirmed; US evidence suggests a test, a recorded video round and then live rounds.
  • KCS case format. No source confirms a "pitch a fund" or "write an investor letter" exercise at KKR. One prep site says a writing exercise "may" be asked. The case drills in this pack are preparation, not prediction.
  • Offer timing for the SEO London cohort, and intern class sizes (estimate only: about 6 to 15 across London teams) are not published.
  • How to rank the six teams. No public advice from KKR or SEO exists; the ranking guidance here is the author's reasoning.

About the firm@@x-firm@@

  • "Industrialist vision" appears in the SEO London listing but was not found in any KKR document read. Do not quote it as KKR's words.
  • Sunset Date. Filings say "no later than 31 December 2026". No announcement that it has happened early was found. Check KKR's 8-K filings before any interview in late 2026 or early 2027.
  • Total London headcount. Only the main UK LLP is quantified (182 average employees and 88 members in FY2025). Other UK entities were not fully read. London estimates (about 300 to 400 people) are inferred.
  • Live FCA Register entries and current approved persons were not checked directly.
  • DOJ settlement (proposed 26 August 2026): court approval not confirmed. Kentucky litigation: 2026 outcome not found.
  • Capstone founding year (often said to be 2000) was not confirmed in a primary source.
  • European Fund VII and Asian Fund V size and closes: not established. Real Estate Partners Europe III: status unclear.
  • Private credit stress at KKR-affiliated vehicles beyond K-FIT's Q1 2026 pro-rated redemptions (for example FS KKR) was not researched.

About the industry and rules@@x-industry@@

  • US 401(k) rule. Only a Department of Labor proposal (30 March 2026) was found; no final rule as of 11 October 2026. SEC accredited-investor proposals (about 30 September 2026) seen only via law-firm summaries.
  • UK CP26/28 publication date differs between sources (14 or about 23 July 2026); consultation closes 14 October 2026.
  • McKinsey and BCG private markets reports were not read directly; their figures are not used.
  • LP-type share of global private capital (pensions vs sovereigns vs insurers vs wealth) for 2026 was not found.
  • Peer facts not verified this session: rivals' tie-ups with traditional managers (relevant to how unique the Capital Group partnership is); rivals' compensation structures (relevant to KKR's "one pool" claim); London client-function internships at Apollo, Ares, Brookfield, TPG, EQT, CVC.
  • Fee norms (2 and 20, 8% hurdle) are textbook norms, not 2026 survey data.

Turn gaps into questions@@x-ask@@

Several gaps are exactly what an insider can answer and an outsider cannot. Asked well, they show research rather than ignorance:

  • "KKR's directory shows coverage by country and by channel in EMEA. Where would a summer analyst sit, and who owns the client when a product specialist and a relationship manager both work on it?"
  • "K-PRIME is the Luxembourg twin of K-PEC. Is there a plan for an ELTIF or an LTAF for UK and EU wealth clients?"
  • "After the Sunset Date, does anything change for how the client team presents KKR's governance to investors?"

Final self-check@@x-check@@

RequirementStatusHow it was met, and where it falls short
Every figure has a source and date; estimates are labelled as estimates on the chartMetEvery data chart caption carries source IDs and an as-of date. Implied or estimated values (for example 2025 AUM bars worked back from growth rates, KCS headcount ranges, intern numbers) carry "est." or a range on the chart and an INFERRED tag in the caption. Conceptual diagrams with no numbers say so ("illustrative").
A total beginner could read the role, firm and industry parts without another sourceMetEvery term is defined in line on first use and again in the glossary (about 120 terms in seven themes). The basics part starts from "what is investing" before any KKR fact.
"Why KKR / why KCS" is mechanism, not adjectives, and would not transplant to a rivalMetThe answer rests on four KKR-specific mechanisms (one P&L and compensation pool; four engines under one client team; KCS and KCM joined by mandate and by one European head; trust as an asset, via Walter Industries). Each has a "don't overclaim" box where rivals have something similar.
The regulatory section is current and dated correctlyMet, two caveatsAIFMD II (OJ 26 Mar 2024, transposition 16 Apr 2026), ELTIF 2.0 (10 Jan 2024), FCA CP26/28 (consultation closes 14 Oct 2026), Pension Schemes Act 2026 (Royal Assent 29 Apr 2026), SEC private fund rules vacated (5 Jun 2024), US EO 14330 (7 Aug 2025) and DOL proposal (30 Mar 2026) were all checked against sources. MiFID II and the UK AIFM Regulations 2013 dates were not re-verified this session.
The team section goes beyond the JD, with method shown and thin evidence admittedMetThe KCS EMEA map names 46 senior people from KKR's own directory (20 in London), with an estimate of 55-90 in total and the scaling method shown. No "Head of KCS EMEA" title exists publicly, and reporting lines are marked as inferred.
Every JD bullet has three scenarios, and the composure set has decision treesMetThe KCS playbook has 11 lines (the seven KCS description lines and the four intern duty lines) with easy, medium and hard cards each (33 cards), and five composure scenarios, three drawn as decision trees. The complete pack adds 30 scenarios across the general duties and testable qualification bullets.
People sections contain only public professional information, with identity uncertainty flaggedMetNames, titles, offices and career paths come from KKR's own biographies and press releases.
